About this document

This TAD describes the architecture behind the first release: the modular monolith, PostgreSQL source of truth, Redis cache, worker, provider interfaces, payments and escrow state machine, double-entry ledger, Goods Flex, search and the frontend. Appendix A is the integration go-live checklist.

1. Architecture principles

  1. Modular monolith first. One deployable API with clear module boundaries and a single database. Scale the process horizontally before splitting services.
  2. Provider interfaces at every regulated or external boundary. Payments, escrow, lending, open banking, identity, storage, SMS and email are behind Protocols so a partner can be replaced without touching domain logic.
  3. Verify before trust. A payment is real only after a server-to-server verification with an exact amount and currency match. Webhooks trigger verification; redirects and screenshots never do.
  4. The database is the source of truth. Financial invariants are enforced by constraints, row locks, unique keys and triggers, not only by application code.
  5. Idempotency everywhere. Checkout, webhooks, settlement, refunds, promotions and BNPL payments can be retried safely.
  6. Same-origin API. The browser talks only to the Next.js origin, which proxies /api/v1 and /media to the backend. This keeps the refresh cookie first-party and removes CORS from the production path.
  7. Operate what you build. Structured logs, request IDs, health checks, reconciliation and audit trails are part of the feature, not an afterthought.

Connection budget
Each API process opens up to DB_POOL_SIZE + DB_MAX_OVERFLOW connections. Total = that × WEB_CONCURRENCY × replicas. Size this against max_connections, or put PgBouncer in front. This is the first thing to tune when adding pods.

5. Backend architecture

The API is a modular monolith. Each module owns its router and business logic; cross-module coupling goes through service functions and the payment purpose registry. The payments module never imports orders, subscriptions or BNPL directly.

LayerResponsibilityExamples
core/Config, DB session, security primitives, errors, JSON logging with request IDs, cache/rate limiter, auth/RBAC dependencies.Argon2, JWT, Fernet, Redis, trusted proxy IP resolution.
models/SQLAlchemy mappings and constraints.Users, sellers, catalog, messaging, commerce, ledger, misc.
integrations/External provider Protocols and adapters.Payments, escrow, BNPL, bank data, identity, storage.
modules/Domain services, routers, state machines, policies.auth, users, sellers, categories, products, subscriptions, messaging, negotiation, payments, orders, promotions, bnpl, reviews, notifications, admin, staff, stats, recommendations, ads, marketing.
worker.pyScheduled jobs with advisory locks.Outbox, expiry, auto-release, subscription/promotion expiry, BNPL reminders, feed/CAPI, purge.

Payment purpose registry

A single payment can satisfy different business purposes: an order, a subscription, a listing promotion, or a BNPL instalment. The payments module activates the correct handler on verified success. This keeps payment verification independent of the domain that initiated it.

PurposeEffect on verified successLedger posting
Order / Protected CheckoutConfirm payment, fund escrow, reserve stock already held, move order to funds safeguarded.Debit provider receipts / credit escrow obligations (via partner mirror).
SubscriptionActivate plan, grant featured credits, set period.Debit provider receipts / credit subscription revenue.
PromotionActivate listing promotion, set tier/featured window.Debit provider receipts / credit promotion revenue.
BNPL instalmentMark instalment paid, update plan status, notify.Recorded against the financing partner's position.

6. Data architecture

54 tables in six domains. Money is Decimal with at most two decimal places and is serialised as a string; it never touches floats. The database enforces the invariants that matter most.

DomainCore tablesKey guarantees
Identity & accessusers, profiles, refresh_tokens, otp_codes, two_factor, admin roles/permissions, staff invitations, audit logsToken rotation and reuse detection; append-only audit; granular RBAC.
Seller & catalogseller_profiles, verifications, categories, products, product_images, favourites, reportsOne seller profile per user; slug uniqueness; image ownership; verification tiers.
Messaging & negotiationconversations, messages, read receipts, negotiations, offersOne live negotiation per buyer/product (partial unique index); stale-offer rejection.
Commerceorders, order_items, payments, escrow_records, escrow_events, refunds, disputes, disputes_messages, reviewsTotal = subtotal + delivery + protection; one active refund; append-only escrow events.
Growthsubscription_plans, subscriptions, promotions, platform_settings, ads/events, interest signalsPremium derived from an active period; promotion tier mirrors an active paid promotion.
Flex & ledgercredit_profiles, bank_connections, credit_assessments, guarantors, applications, agreements, instalments, ledger_accounts, ledger_transactions, ledger_entriesOne running plan; guarantor cap; immutable assessment snapshots; balanced ledger at commit.

Ledger design

The ledger is double-entry and append-only. A deferred constraint trigger rejects any unbalanced transaction at commit. Database triggers block updates and deletes on ledger, escrow-event and audit tables.

EventDebitCredit
Escrow fundedasset:escrow_partner_holdingliability:escrow_obligations
Released to sellerliability:escrow_obligationsliability:seller_payable:<seller>, revenue:platform_commission, revenue:protection_fees
Refundedliability:escrow_obligationsasset:escrow_partner_holding
Subscriptionasset:provider_receiptsrevenue:subscriptions
Promotionasset:provider_receiptsrevenue:promotions

7. API architecture

  • Style: REST under /api/v1; JSON; 185 endpoints; OpenAPI in development/test only.
  • Auth: Bearer access token (15 min) plus an httpOnly refresh cookie scoped to /api/v1/auth; CSRF header on cookie-authenticated endpoints.
  • Idempotency: Idempotency-Key on checkout; unique (provider, event_key) on webhooks; unique ledger keys on settlement.
  • Errors: consistent {error:{code,message,details}}; resource ownership failures return 404 to avoid existence leaks.
  • Rate limits: per user/device and a coarse per-IP ceiling (20× by default) for carrier NAT; stricter per-action limits on login, OTP, offers, messages, uploads, checkout and Flex.
  • Webhooks: POST /api/v1/payments/webhooks/{provider}/webhook; signatures verified (Paystack HMAC-SHA512, Flutterwave verif-hash); invalid signatures return 403; events de-duplicated.
  • Health: /health for liveness, /health/ready checks the database and reports providers outside production.

8. Identity and access

ControlImplementation
PasswordsArgon2id; automatic re-hash on login; 8+ characters with letters and digits; timing-safe login for unknown emails.
Access tokensShort-lived JWT (15 min) kept in memory; algorithm pinned to HS256/384/512; per-user token version revokes all on password/role/status change.
Refresh tokensOpaque, hashed at rest, rotated on every use; reuse revokes the family; httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure outside development.
OTP6 digits, HMAC-peppered, 10-minute TTL, 5 attempts, 3 sends/10 min and 10/day per number.
2FATOTP with single-use recovery codes and replay protection; required for admins in production; staff cannot use Google sign-in.
CaptchareCAPTCHA v2 or Turnstile, enforced before the password check for new devices (24 h) or after 3 wrong passwords.
Google sign-inOIDC web flow; mock consent in development; hidden in production when credentials are absent.
RBACGranular admin permissions; only super admins change roles; every admin route has a permission dependency; audit log is append-only.
Proxy trustX-Forwarded-For ignored unless the peer is in TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS; chain walked right-to-left.

9. Payments, escrow and ledger

Goods.ng does not hold funds. A licensed escrow/payment partner holds them; Goods.ng instructs release or refund based on the order state machine. The ledger mirrors the partner's position.

pending_payment ─▶ payment_confirmed ─▶ funds_safeguarded ─▶ awaiting_seller ─▶ processing ─▶ dispatched │ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ cancelled refund_pending ◀── (decline/cancel) delivered │ │ ▼ ▼ refunded completed ◀─ awaiting_buyer_confirmation ▲ │ disputed ──────────────┘ (admin) │ (auto-release after N days)
  • Verify before trust: server-to-server verify with exact amount and currency; webhook signature; redirects never trusted.
  • No double settlement: state machine + row locks + unique escrow:<id>:settle ledger key; a five-thread concurrency test asserts one settlement.
  • Server-side pricing: totals from the listing or an accepted negotiation owned by the buyer; DB check constraint on the total.
  • Stock: reserved atomically at checkout; restored on unpaid expiry or pre-dispatch refund; late payment honoured if stock remains, otherwise auto-refunded.
  • Refunds: automatic pre-dispatch for cancellation/decline; dispute refunds need a second, different admin; one active refund per order.
  • Reconciliation: /admin/reconciliation cross-checks payments, escrow states and ledger postings.

10. Goods Flex

Flex is a credit product, not a wallet. Before applying, the customer builds a credit profile: verified phone → BVN (Fernet-encrypted, keyed fingerprint to prevent reuse) → read-only bank connection → mandatory guarantor consent → optional workplace verification. Without a guarantor, the limit is zero and no application can start.

StepRule
Bank assessmentSix months of transactions; salary detection or 70% of median eligible inflow; deduct existing repayments; risk factor from volatility, missing months, betting share and failed debits.
Limitmin(statement limit, verification-tier cap, repayment-history cap, lender maximum); zero without phone + BVN + bank + consented guarantor.
GuarantorSees borrower, relationship, amount and expiry; explicit consent; consent time, IP and BVN reference recorded; amount caps the limit; at most 3 active guarantees per person; withdrawal drops the limit to zero.
DecisionPartner decision stored with reference; offer terms stored verbatim; buyer explicitly accepts.
One planOnly one of approved/accepted/active/defaulted at a time, enforced in the service under a row lock and by a partial unique index.
FundsDown payment via the payment layer; partner disburses; order funded through the same escrow path; refund cancels the agreement.
RepaymentInstalments via the payment layer; worker marks overdue and reminds; defaulted plans can still be paid off.

11. Search and discovery

  • Engine: PostgreSQL full-text search; generated weighted tsvector (title A, brand/model B, description C) with a GIN index and prefix matching (iph matches iPhone).
  • Ranking: featured first, then premium sellers, then text rank, then recency.
  • Filters/facets: state, category, price, condition, brand, BNPL, delivery, verification; counts computed for the current result set.
  • Sponsored: premium sellers and Boost Premium listings enter a quality-gated sponsored pool; TOP promotes a single listing.
  • Seam: products.service.search() is the single place to swap in a dedicated engine later.
  • Recommendations: interest signals and a "for you" feed; purge job keeps signal tables bounded.

12. Messaging and negotiation

AreaBehaviour
ConversationsProduct-linked; one thread per buyer/seller/product context; read receipts and unread counts; 5-second polling while visible, paused when hidden.
SafetyDirect-contact warning gate; message reporting; rate limits; HTML stripped.
NegotiationOne live negotiation per buyer/product; turn-taking; counter direction; minimum offer 10% of list; 48-hour offer expiry; 24-hour checkout after acceptance; 10-round cap.
ConcurrencyEvery response locks the negotiation row and must name the pending offer; stale/double clicks get 409 stale_offer.
Price integrityThe public listing price never changes; the accepted offer becomes the checkout price for that buyer only.

13. Frontend architecture

  • Public pages (home, search, category, item, store, info) are server-rendered with streaming and PPR; static shells are prerendered; JSON-LD, canonical URLs, OG metadata, sitemap and robots are included.
  • Dashboards (account, orders, messages, seller, admin) are client components on a central API client: in-memory access token, silent refresh through the httpOnly cookie with a CSRF header, one retry on 401.
  • Performance: system fonts, backend WebP thumbnails (400 px) and full images (1280 px), lazy loading, skeletons, Redis-cached feeds, bottom navigation on phones.
  • Admin host: frontend/src/proxy.ts serves the console on admin.goods.ng, redirects /admin/..., and adds X-Robots-Tag: noindex. Sessions are per host.
  • Resilience: no client-side price trust, no direct provider secrets, and no analytics scripts before marketing consent.

14. Media pipeline

  1. Input capped at MAX_UPLOAD_MB (8 MB) and 40 MP (decompression-bomb guard).
  2. Decoded with Pillow; extension and MIME are not trusted.
  3. Re-encoded to WebP: full at 1280 px, thumbnail at 400 px; EXIF/GPS and embedded payloads stripped.
  4. Listing photos watermarked with the seller business name and Goods.ng.
  5. Stored under random keys; public media to S3 + CDN; KYC documents to the private prefix with server-side encryption and short-lived signed URLs.
  6. Per-seller cap MAX_IMAGES_PER_SELLER (200); soft-deleted listings purged after 30 days.

16. Caching and performance

  • Cache: Redis with an in-memory development fallback; anonymous search cached for 15 s; public feeds cached; single-flight locks prevent stampedes.
  • Rate limiting: per user/device and a coarse per-IP ceiling; hot paths use constant-time checks.
  • Database: 15 s statement timeout, 60 s idle-in-transaction timeout, pooled connections, indexes for search and browse.
  • Measurement: k6 realistic mix; single dev worker plateaus at ~182 req/s. Add workers/replicas and PgBouncer before that becomes the ceiling.

18. Observability and operations

  • Logs: structured JSON on stdout with request_id on every line and in the x-request-id response header; ship to a log platform.
  • Health: /health (liveness) and /health/ready (DB, cache, providers outside production).
  • Error tracking: Sentry SDK for FastAPI and Next.js is not wired yet; add DSNs via secrets and extend CSP allowlists.
  • Alerting: 5xx rate, p95 latency, readiness failures, worker job failures, payment amount mismatch, invalid webhook signatures, non-empty reconciliation, overdue BNPL growth, guarantor limit spikes, provider errors, bank-connection drop.
  • Backups: managed PITR 7–35 days plus encrypted daily logical dumps to a separate account/region; quarterly restore drill into staging and ledger reconciliation.
  • Rollback: redeploy the previous immutable image tag; prefer forward database fixes; never blindly downgrade financial tables.

20. Scalability plan

  1. Horizontal API: add replicas; keep the app stateless; move sessions/tokens as already designed.
  2. Database: PgBouncer transaction pooling; read replicas for browse/search; partition large event tables if needed; then shard only as a last resort.
  3. Cache: increase Redis capacity; add per-entity cache invalidation; cache anonymous feeds and facets.
  4. Search: move to a dedicated engine when Postgres FTS p95 or query complexity becomes the bottleneck.
  5. Messaging: WebSockets/SSE or a managed pub/sub when polling at scale becomes expensive.
  6. Media: CDN offload, responsive variants, signed URLs; keep origin egress low.
  7. Worker: more replicas are safe; split jobs by queue if contention appears.

21. Architecture decisions

ADRDecisionRationale
001Modular monolith, not microservicesSmall team, shared transactions, fast iteration; module seams allow later extraction.
002PostgreSQL as the only source of truthStrong constraints, transactions, FTS and operational simplicity; ledger integrity is paramount.
003Provider interfaces for regulated servicesPartners change; the domain must not. Production refuses mocks.
004Same-origin API via Next.js rewriteFirst-party refresh cookie, no CORS, simpler CSP, better mobile reliability.
005Double-entry ledger with DB triggersMoney correctness cannot depend on application discipline alone.
006Verify-before-trust paymentsWebhooks and redirects are signals, not proof.
007Premium is derived, not storedAn active subscription period is the only truth; clients cannot self-grant.
008Per-listing promotions separate from subscriptionsLowers the barrier: a seller can buy visibility for one product without a plan.
009Postgres FTS firstSufficient at launch; one seam to replace later.
010Polling messaging firstSimpler operations; WebSockets can replace without API changes.

14Malware scanningScan listing images and KYC documents before storage/access.NOT BUILTClamAV or cloud scanner; quarantine bucket; scan status; admin review; alerting.YesSecurity
15Logistics / carrierLabels, pickup and tracking events for dispatched orders.NOT BUILT manual tracking fieldsAt least one carrier (GIGL, DHL, Sendbox, etc.); label API; tracking webhooks; status mapping; failed-delivery flow.NoOps + Eng
16Google Merchant Center + AdsProduct listing ads and Shopping/Performance Max campaigns.CONFIG feed endpointMerchant Center; claim goods.ng; Nigeria/NGN; scheduled fetch; link Ads; campaign; feed quality checks.NoGrowth
17Meta Pixel / Catalog / CAPICatalog ads and consented server-side purchase events.CONFIG pixel, feed, CAPI codeBusiness Manager; catalog data source; domain verification; pixel ID; CAPI token; campaign; event dedup check.NoGrowth
18GA4 / Google Ads tagsAcquisition and conversion measurement.CONFIG settings + consent gateProperty/tag IDs; conversion labels; consent mode; verify no scripts before consent.NoGrowth
19Google OAuthOptional social sign-in.CONFIG implemented, mock in devOAuth web client; consent screen; redirect URIs; publish/verify app; privacy/terms links.NoEng
20Push notificationsRe-engage buyers/sellers; required for future native apps.NOT BUILTFCM/APNs; device tokens; preferences; deep links; delivery analytics.NoEng
21WhatsApp Business APIStructured messaging and template notifications.NOT BUILT deep links onlyCloud API; number; templates; opt-in; webhook; human handoff; 24-hour window handling.NoGrowth + Eng
22Dedicated searchSearch relevance and latency at scale.NOT BUILT Postgres FTSOpenSearch/Meilisearch; index pipeline; ranking parity; A/B; swap behind service.search().NoEng
23WebSockets / SSELower-latency messaging if polling becomes costly.NOT BUILT 5 s pollingGateway; auth; fan-out; presence; reconnect; load test; mobile background behaviour.NoEng
24Fraud / risk scoringDetect abusive signups, listings and payments.NOT BUILT rules onlyVendor or in-house scoring; device fingerprint; velocity rules; manual review queue; model governance.NoTrust & Safety
25NDPA / DPO toolingData-subject export/delete, retention and processing records.PARTIAL copy onlyDSR workflow; retention jobs; record of processing; DPO appointment; processor agreements; breach playbook.YesCompliance

* Mono is not a production boot blocker, but Goods Flex cannot go live without it (or another open-banking provider) because the credit limit depends on a real bank assessment. If Flex is feature-flagged off at launch, Mono can follow.

Top five blockers, in order
1. Licensed escrow/payment partner (Protected Checkout cannot launch without it). 2. Licensed lender (Goods Flex cannot launch without it). 3. Payment provider certification (no live money). 4. Production deployment + managed infrastructure (nothing is live). 5. KYC + SMS/email + captcha (security and account recovery).

B. Environment variables

VariablePurpose / production requirement
ENVIRONMENTdevelopment | test | staging | production. Controls boot guards and dev routes.
DATABASE_URLPostgreSQL DSN; must use sslmode=require/verify-full in production.
DB_POOL_SIZE / DB_MAX_OVERFLOW / DB_POOL_TIMEOUTPer-process pool; size against Postgres max_connections or PgBouncer.
REDIS_URLRequired in production; shared cache, rate limits, single-flight.
JWT_SECRET / OTP_SECRET / DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEYUnique per environment; production rejects dev defaults; back up the Fernet key.
FRONTEND_URL / CORS_ORIGINS / ADMIN_URLExplicit https origins; admin subdomain used in staff invites.
TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRSLoad balancer CIDRs; required in production for correct client IPs.
ADMIN_2FA_REQUIREDMust be true in production; admins enable TOTP before using the admin API.
PAYMENT_PROVIDERmock | paystack | flutterwave; mock refused in production.
ESCROW_PROVIDER / BNPL_PROVIDERMock only today; production refuses mock; real adapters required.
BANK_DATA_PROVIDER / MONO_* mock | mono; Mono keys server-side only; production refuses mock.
PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY / FLUTTERWAVE_*Provider credentials and webhook hash.
SMS_PROVIDER / TERMII_*console | termii; production refuses console.
EMAIL_PROVIDER / SMTP_* / POSTMARK_*console | smtp | postmark; production refuses console.
STORAGE_BACKEND / S3_* / MEDIA_BASE_URLlocal | s3; production requires s3 + bucket; CDN URL for media.
CAPTCHA_PROVIDER / *_SITE_KEY / *_SECRET_KEYoff | mock | recaptcha | turnstile; production refuses mock/off.
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / SECRETGoogle OAuth; hidden in production when absent.
META_CAPI_ACCESS_TOKEN / META_GRAPH_VERSIONServer-side purchase events; token never in DB/client.
FEED_TOKENOptional protection for Google/Meta feeds.
PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE / PROTECTION_FEE_RATE / PROTECTION_FEE_CAPMarketplace economics; admin-overridable.
AUTO_RELEASE_DAYSBuyer-confirmation window before escrow release (default 3).
RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE / RATE_LIMIT_IP_MULTIPLIERPer-identity and coarse per-IP ceilings.
MAX_UPLOAD_MB / MAX_IMAGES_PER_SELLER / DELETED_LISTING_RETENTION_DAYSMedia abuse and retention controls.
RATE_LIMIT_MULTIPLIERDev/test only; must be 1 outside development.

C. Glossary

TermMeaning
Protected CheckoutGoods.ng checkout where a licensed partner holds the buyer's funds until delivery is confirmed or the dispute process resolves.
Escrow partnerA licensed third party that holds and releases funds. Goods.ng does not hold funds.
Goods FlexBuy-now-pay-later product with an affordability assessment, mandatory guarantor and instalments.
GuarantorA person who consents to cover a Flex borrower's obligation up to a stated, capped amount.
Premium sellerDerived status from an active paid subscription; unlocks contact buttons, analytics, banner and ranking.
PromotionA one-off paid visibility package for a single listing: TOP 7, TOP 30 or Boost Premium 28.
Boost PremiumPromotion tier that makes a listing eligible for the sponsored pool while it meets quality gates.
LedgerDouble-entry, append-only record of money movements; balanced at commit by a deferred trigger.
Seller payableLedger liability representing money owed to a seller after release, before disbursement.
Verify-before-trustServer-to-server payment verification with exact amount/currency; webhooks are only triggers.
IdempotencyThe property that retrying the same request has no additional effect.
Four-eyesA second, different admin must approve a dispute refund.
NDPANigeria Data Protection Act 2023.
FCCPCFederal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission; regulates digital lending conduct.
CBNCentral Bank of Nigeria; licenses payment/escrow institutions.
PPRPartial Prerendering (Next.js); static shell with streamed dynamic data.
FTSPostgreSQL full-text search.
PgBouncerConnection pooler used in front of Postgres at scale.
PITRPoint-in-time recovery for the database.
